super-metroid.summary: Samus returns to Zebes, gaining abilities that open new routes through its interconnected world.
super-metroid.review: Super Metroid lets the world do much of the talking. A sealed door or unreachable ledge becomes a reason to keep exploring; its controls show their age, but its spatial design remains compelling.
super-metroid.fit: Players who enjoy reading maps, remembering branches and revisiting old paths with new abilities.
super-metroid.caution: Some controls and hidden passages have little modern guidance.
super-metroid.replay: A compact route and completion-time goals invite repeat runs.

metroid-dread.summary: Samus explores planet ZDR while evading E.M.M.I. pursuers and unlocking new routes.
metroid-dread.review: Responsive movement and E.M.M.I. chases give Dread a strong forward pull. It suits players who want a brisker action rhythm, though the pursuit sequences can feel intense.
metroid-dread.fit: Players who like precise combat, fast movement and a clear sense of progress.
metroid-dread.caution: Chases and bosses may take repeated attempts.
metroid-dread.replay: Harder modes and completion-time goals reward more efficient routes.

castlevania-symphony-of-the-night.summary: Explore Dracula's castle as Alucard, using equipment, spells and transformations to uncover its secrets.
castlevania-symphony-of-the-night.review: The castle rewards patient digging: gear, transformations and hidden rooms keep yielding discoveries. Combat balance is often forgiving; the exploratory mood is the stronger draw.
castlevania-symphony-of-the-night.fit: Players drawn to castle atmosphere, equipment collecting and gradual map discovery.
castlevania-symphony-of-the-night.caution: The older interface and some concealed routes demand patience.
castlevania-symphony-of-the-night.replay: Hidden outcomes and optional play styles add reasons to revisit the castle.

castlevania-aria-of-sorrow.summary: Soma explores a mysterious castle and gains abilities by collecting enemy souls.
castlevania-aria-of-sorrow.review: The soul system makes even ordinary enemies interesting: each may offer a new ability. Its compact length makes it an approachable entry to exploration-focused Castlevania.
castlevania-aria-of-sorrow.fit: Players who like collecting abilities and testing combinations in a focused adventure.
castlevania-aria-of-sorrow.caution: Some souls depend on random drops.
castlevania-aria-of-sorrow.replay: Different endings and an additional character mode offer a fresh route.

bloodstained-ritual-of-the-night.summary: Explore a demon-filled castle as Miriam, opening routes with equipment and shard abilities.
bloodstained-ritual-of-the-night.review: Bloodstained offers a broad mix of gear, shards and castle exploration. There is plenty to experiment with, though collecting materials and managing menus take time.
bloodstained-ritual-of-the-night.fit: Players who enjoy builds, equipment and a large castle to explore.
bloodstained-ritual-of-the-night.caution: Its many systems may feel busy if you want pure platform action.
bloodstained-ritual-of-the-night.replay: Optional modes, collection goals and different ability builds support repeat play.

castlevania-belmonts-curse.summary: An upcoming 2D Castlevania adventure starring Rose Belmont, set after Dracula's Curse.
castlevania-belmonts-curse.review: Traversal is packed with spikes, saw blades and precision-platforming challenges. Change the visuals and characters, and it could easily bring Hollow Knight to mind. Many walls that change with different states are familiar tricks from other platformers, too. Add the highly aggressive enemies along the way, and it starts to feel like Dead Cells. Smaller details such as skills and equipment also draw on mechanics common in popular games. For me, its biggest problem is that, as a new Castlevania, it may differ from earlier Castlevania games, but its gameplay does not feel particularly new.
castlevania-belmonts-curse.fit: Players interested in a new 2D Castlevania can follow its release and later coverage.
castlevania-belmonts-curse.caution: Play time, difficulty and replay features remain unverified.
castlevania-belmonts-curse.replay: Replay features will be checked after release.

hollow-knight.summary: Descend into Hallownest, explore its connected regions and uncover new ways to move.
hollow-knight.review: Hollow Knight makes exploration its own reward. A wrong turn can reveal a character, a secret or an entirely new place, while its hand-drawn world stays with you. The sparse guidance and demanding bosses are part of the experience.
hollow-knight.fit: Players who enjoy finding their own route, revisiting maps and learning boss patterns.
hollow-knight.caution: You will get lost, and some platforming and boss encounters need practice.
hollow-knight.replay: Different endings and challenge content offer reasons to return without ability-carryover NG+.

hollow-knight-silksong.summary: Explore a new kingdom as Hornet in the follow-up to Hollow Knight.
hollow-knight-silksong.review: Hornet moves and fights with a more assertive rhythm than the Knight. Discovery still drives the journey, but action demands more attention from the start.
hollow-knight-silksong.fit: Players comfortable with demanding exploration and boss practice.
hollow-knight-silksong.caution: The first game's combat habits do not transfer directly.
hollow-knight-silksong.replay: Additional challenges and completion goals reward route and combat mastery.

ori-and-the-blind-forest.summary: Guide Ori through Nibel, learning movement abilities to cross the forest.
ori-and-the-blind-forest.review: Ori's fluid movement, art and music carry the adventure. Platforming takes center stage, and its escape sequences can be the hardest moments.
ori-and-the-blind-forest.fit: Players who enjoy expressive platforming and an emotional audiovisual journey.
ori-and-the-blind-forest.caution: Timed escapes may require repeated practice.
ori-and-the-blind-forest.replay: Collectibles and cleaner routes are the main reasons to replay.

ori-and-the-will-of-the-wisps.summary: Explore a wider world with Ori through platforming, combat, puzzles and new abilities.
ori-and-the-will-of-the-wisps.review: The sequel keeps Ori's flowing traversal while expanding combat and side activities. It offers more choices, at the cost of a busier set of systems.
ori-and-the-will-of-the-wisps.fit: Players who want platforming, exploration and richer combat together.
ori-and-the-will-of-the-wisps.caution: Some challenges still demand precise movement.
ori-and-the-will-of-the-wisps.replay: Collections, side activities and challenges extend the journey.

islets.summary: Travel between separated islands as Iko and reconnect a gradually opening world.
islets.review: Islets keeps exploration light and welcoming. Connecting its islands changes the map as you play, making it a good choice for discovery without prolonged difficulty spikes.
islets.fit: Players who want approachable exploration and a relatively short adventure.
islets.caution: It may feel slight if you want deep builds or severe combat challenges.
islets.replay: Return for collectibles or try a quicker route.

crypt-custodian.summary: Explore the afterlife as Pluto the cat, solving puzzles and gaining new abilities.
crypt-custodian.review: Its top-down perspective gives revisiting the map a different feel. Broom combat and a playful afterlife setting preserve the approachable character of Kyle Thompson's games.
crypt-custodian.fit: Players who like top-down exploration, light puzzles and characterful stories.
crypt-custodian.caution: Expect a different perspective from traditional side-scrolling platformers.
crypt-custodian.replay: Map completion and collectibles are clearer reasons to return than a dedicated second run.

ender-lilies.summary: Explore a world ruined by the Rain of Death and fight with the spirits you purify.
ender-lilies.review: Dark visuals and music establish a powerful mood, while spirit skills keep combat flexible. Exploration and bosses both ask for patience.
ender-lilies.fit: Players who enjoy dark fantasy, skill combinations and boss challenges.
ender-lilies.caution: Some bosses and routes may be frustrating.
ender-lilies.replay: Endings, collections and skill builds add depth without requiring a fresh run.

ender-magnolia.summary: Explore a smoke-stricken land with Lilac and her artificial companions, decades after Ender Lilies.
ender-magnolia.review: The follow-up retains companion abilities and a somber world while making movement and combat more immediate.
ender-magnolia.fit: Players seeking companion skills, boss fights and a readable growth path.
ender-magnolia.caution: Combat still has a learning curve, and the story connects to its predecessor.
ender-magnolia.replay: Collections and skill combinations extend play; dedicated replay mechanics need checking.

afterimage.summary: Explore the hand-drawn world of Engardin with varied weapons and abilities.
afterimage.review: Afterimage stands out for its scale: regions, weapons and branching choices give long-term explorers plenty to do. The map and systems can feel dense early on.
afterimage.fit: Players who enjoy large maps, weapon choices and a long progression arc.
afterimage.caution: Navigation and system knowledge take time to build.
afterimage.replay: Alternate endings and later content provide reasons to continue.

deaths-door.summary: Play a soul-reaping crow through connected worlds, dungeons, puzzles and boss fights.
deaths-door.review: Death's Door combines top-down combat, lean puzzles and dry humor with a steady pace. Its routes are more focused than a typical metroidvania.
deaths-door.fit: Players who want a concise top-down action adventure.
deaths-door.caution: Combat gives limited room for error, and some collectibles require revisits.
deaths-door.replay: Post-game exploration and hidden content are the main reasons to return.

tunic.summary: Explore an unfamiliar world as a small fox, learning its rules from scattered manual pages.
tunic.review: TUNIC's central pleasure is understanding. Each manual page can change how you see the world; players who want explicit instructions may find it opaque.
tunic.fit: Players who enjoy interpreting clues and discovering hidden rules.
tunic.caution: Later knowledge puzzles are demanding, and combat is not always gentle.
tunic.replay: A New Game+ exists, though pursuing secrets in the first save may be more rewarding.

metroid-fusion.summary: Investigate the X parasite aboard a space station while evading the dangerous SA-X.
metroid-fusion.review: The station and SA-X make Fusion tenser than some other Metroid games. Its directed route favors narrative momentum over open-ended wandering.
metroid-fusion.fit: Players who like compact sci-fi suspense and clear stages of progress.
metroid-fusion.caution: Exploration is more constrained, and chases create pressure.
metroid-fusion.replay: Clear time and collection rate offer goals for repeat runs.

castlevania-dawn-of-sorrow.summary: Soma returns in the sequel to Aria of Sorrow, collecting souls as he explores another castle.
castlevania-dawn-of-sorrow.review: Dawn of Sorrow expands on soul collection and equipment growth. Finding new powers remains satisfying, though the grind becomes more visible.
castlevania-dawn-of-sorrow.fit: Players who like soul builds, castle exploration and character growth.
castlevania-dawn-of-sorrow.caution: Some souls take repeated attempts; the original uses touch controls.
castlevania-dawn-of-sorrow.replay: An additional character mode and collection goals change repeat runs.

blasphemous.summary: Travel through Cvstodia as the Penitent One, fighting and uncovering relics and secrets.
blasphemous.review: Religious imagery and heavy pixel art give Blasphemous a distinct identity. Combat rewards caution, while its story asks you to assemble clues yourself.
blasphemous.fit: Players drawn to striking art, secrets and punishing fights.
blasphemous.caution: Violent religious imagery and difficult combat are central to its tone.
blasphemous.replay: Additional challenges and endings provide reasons for another run.

blasphemous-2.summary: The Penitent One wakes in a new world, exploring with multiple weapons and abilities.
blasphemous-2.review: The sequel binds weapon choice more closely to opening paths, making progress through its map especially tangible. Its intense visual and combat style remains.
blasphemous-2.fit: Players who want weapon variety and ability-gated exploration.
blasphemous-2.caution: Bosses and platform challenges still require practice.
blasphemous-2.replay: Return for collections and endings; check the version played for replay updates.

nine-sols.summary: Explore New Kunlun in a Taoist science-fiction adventure built around parries and counterattacks.
nine-sols.review: Nine Sols puts parry timing at the center of combat. Learning that rhythm makes major duels rewarding, but the action threshold is high.
nine-sols.fit: Players who enjoy practicing parries and hard-won boss victories.
nine-sols.caution: Repeatedly learning attack timing is part of the main path.
nine-sols.replay: Other challenge goals exist; dedicated replay mechanics need version-specific checking.

animal-well.summary: Search a layered well for items and clues, experimenting with hidden uses and puzzles.
animal-well.review: Animal Well treats curiosity as a core skill. Items often do more than they first appear to, rewarding observation rather than a checklist.
animal-well.fit: Players who like sparse hints, hidden systems and testing ideas.
animal-well.caution: Its deepest secrets can be extremely obscure.
animal-well.replay: Its depth lies mostly in solving more puzzles after the first ending.

souldiers.summary: Choose a class and explore Terragaya in a long pixel-art action RPG adventure.
souldiers.review: Pixel art, class choice and RPG growth are the main draw. Its length favors players willing to work through demanding fights and repeated exploration.
souldiers.fit: Players who like class differences and lengthy pixel-art adventures.
souldiers.caution: Both combat and platforming can become barriers.
souldiers.replay: Class choice encourages a new run; carryover rules need checking.

another-crabs-treasure.summary: Help Kril search an underwater kingdom for his lost shell, using found objects as armor.
another-crabs-treasure.review: A bright underwater world and playful writing frame its soulslike combat. New shells are both defensive choices and a source of discovery; the cute look does not remove the challenge.
another-crabs-treasure.fit: Players curious about soulslike combat who enjoy humor and colorful worlds.
another-crabs-treasure.caution: Bosses still require pattern learning, and some areas test your jumps.
another-crabs-treasure.replay: Return for exploration and collectibles; the main story does not demand another run.

ai-limit.summary: Explore a ruined future city as the regenerated mech Arisa, searching for the truth of its collapse.
ai-limit.review: AI LIMIT builds a clear science-fiction identity around its ruined city and protagonist. Regional exploration and weapon combat reward learning its rhythm.
ai-limit.fit: Players who enjoy post-apocalyptic science fiction and soulslike exploration.
ai-limit.caution: Bosses and resource management can be demanding.
ai-limit.replay: Other weapons and routes invite experimentation; carryover rules need checking.

an-jing-wei-guang.summary: Guide a matchstick-carrying bird through a dark fairy-tale kingdom.
an-jing-wei-guang.review: The bird and matchstick create a memorable fairy-tale image, continuing Kyle Thompson's hand-drawn style. This site's guide remains in progress; the verdict will grow with verified play notes.
an-jing-wei-guang.fit: Players drawn to hand-drawn worlds, new movement abilities and character stories.
an-jing-wei-guang.caution: Detailed route and difficulty notes are still being verified.

the-first-berserker-khazan.summary: Play as the exiled general Khazan in a demanding action RPG built around defense, stamina and boss fights.
the-first-berserker-khazan.review: Khazan puts combat rhythm first: read an enemy's movement, manage stamina and look for a safe opening to counterattack. Our independent guide is in progress, and route and collectible notes will expand after verification.
the-first-berserker-khazan.fit: Players who enjoy demanding action and learning boss patterns through repeated attempts.
the-first-berserker-khazan.caution: Mistakes in combat can be costly; detailed routes and collectibles are still being documented.
the-first-berserker-khazan.replay: Carryover and extra content in subsequent runs await hands-on verification.

grime.summary: Explore a surreal organic world, absorb enemy attacks and traits with a black hole, and combine living weapons with ability progression in timing-focused combat.
grime.review: Not hands-on reviewed. The official description makes absorption and parrying central to both combat and character builds. Organic environments and living weapons give it a distinctive identity; it may suit players who enjoy learning enemy patterns and exploring patiently.
grime.fit: Fans of surreal art, Souls-like combat, parry counters and ability-gated exploration.
grime.caution: Contains body horror and transforming anatomy. Combat emphasizes timing; suitability depends on personal preferences.
grime.replay: The official store confirms New Game Plus with altered enemy and boss challenges, a secret boss, and continued weapon and trait progression.

castlevania-grimoire-of-souls.summary: Play as Alucard, Simon and other series heroes through side-scrolling stages with character skills and equipment progression. Primarily a mobile title; the Apple Arcade version ended service on September 3, 2026.
castlevania-grimoire-of-souls.review: Not hands-on reviewed. Distinct combat styles and skills for familiar Castlevania characters are its main appeal in the official description. This catalog records it as a stage-based mobile entry in the series.
castlevania-grimoire-of-souls.fit: Fans of Alucard, Simon and the history of Castlevania’s mobile games.
castlevania-grimoire-of-souls.caution: The Apple Arcade version has ended service; this is a historical catalog entry. The two-character video scene may be from an earlier version and does not establish multiplayer support in later versions.
castlevania-grimoire-of-souls.replay: Built around stage challenges and equipment progression. Traditional New Game Plus is not confirmed by the referenced official material. Service has ended.

aggelos.summary: Explore the Kingdom of Lumen in a retro pixel-art action RPG, gaining elemental powers through forests, caves and temples to open new paths with swordplay and magic.
aggelos.review: Not hands-on reviewed. The official description combines retro pixel art, swordplay and elemental powers with nonlinear exploration. It may appeal to players who enjoy Wonder Boy-style action adventures.
aggelos.fit: Fans of retro pixel art, dungeon exploration and returning to earlier areas with new abilities.
aggelos.caution: This assessment is based on official gameplay descriptions. Controls, actual difficulty and first-playthrough length remain to be verified.
aggelos.replay: Traditional New Game Plus is not confirmed by the referenced store material.

astlibra-revision.summary: Journey through time and fate with Karon, a talking bird companion. Explore chapter-based worlds, fight side-scrolling battles and develop your character through equipment mastery and skill combinations.
astlibra-revision.review: Not hands-on reviewed. Official descriptions link chapter-based storytelling, side-scrolling combat and character builds. Equipment mastery and skill combinations provide room to adjust playstyles; it may suit action RPG players who enjoy story progression and character growth.
astlibra-revision.fit: Fans of chapter-based stories, equipment progression, skill combinations and side-scrolling combat.
astlibra-revision.caution: Multiple difficulty options are available; actual difficulty remains to be verified. A chapter-by-chapter guide is advisable to avoid spoilers in its time-and-fate narrative.
astlibra-revision.replay: The official description confirms a Postscript after the Final Chapter with additional story, adventure and systems. This is not confirmation of traditional New Game Plus.
